metadata.scenario_context: Zachary unexpectedly finds herself expecting a child with her fiancé, and they accelerate their wedding plans.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Indonesia strongly disagree that abortion is not justifiable.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia strongly agree that abortion is not justifiable.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bring  white lilies as a gift
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is reasonable to get abortion.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide on an appropriate gift for Zachary upcoming nuptials.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is reasonable to get abortion.

shared_prefix.speaker: Melissa, a 24-year-old Spanish-Indonesian mix, pursuing her Masters degree.
shared_prefix.message: Hey Elaine, I was thinking... since Zachary is expecting, maybe I could bring some white lilies as a gift for her. What do you think? They symbolize purity and new beginnings, which feels fitting for her situation.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Elaine, a 29-year-old anthropologist from Indonesia.
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... I see your point about the symbolism. But in my culture, it’s common to give something more practical for weddings. Maybe something like a nice kitchen appliance or something for their new home? I think that would be more meaningful for her new life. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Melissa, a 24-year-old Spanish-Indonesian mix, pursuing her Masters degree.
shared_prefix.message: I get that, but I really feel like white lilies have a special significance, especially right now. They're beautiful and represent hope... I just think they’d be a lovely gesture. By the way, have you thought about whether getting an abortion is reasonable for her? I can't help but wonder if it's an option she should consider.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Elaine, a 29-year-old anthropologist from Indonesia.
shared_prefix.message: I appreciate your thoughts on the lilies, but I still believe something practical would be better. As for the abortion question, in my culture, we strongly believe that it is not justifiable. Zachary is expecting a child, and I think it's important to embrace that life and support her in this journey. What do you think about focusing on how to celebrate her wedding instead?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Melissa, a 24-year-old Spanish-Indonesian mix, pursuing her Masters degree.
shared_prefix.message: I understand your perspective on practical gifts, but I still feel strongly about the significance of the lilies. They really resonate with the situation. Regarding abortion, I just can’t agree with the idea that it’s justifiable. Life is precious, and supporting her in this journey feels so important. Celebrating her wedding is definitely part of it, but I think we should also keep the conversation about her choices open.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Elaine, a 29-year-old anthropologist from Indonesia.
shared_prefix.message: I really appreciate your perspective on the lilies, and I see that they hold a lot of meaning for you. It's great that we can share our thoughts so openly. When it comes to the idea of abortion, I think we can agree that at the core, every person values life and wants what's best for the future, right? Deep down, we are all the same in wanting to support each other during difficult times. I believe that embracing this pregnancy is part of that support. We both know, at the end of the day, we're focused on what's best for Zachary and her family.
